title: What a body presents to a field object: the source at first order in the coupling

key_results.statement: For every product start, to first order in $\gamma$ at fixed $\lambda$: $i\,\mathrm dV_f/\mathrm d\lambda=[G_f,V_f]+R_f$, $G_f=C_f+\sum_xs_x(\lambda)\Phi_x$, source field $s_x=\gamma\langle\xi(\lambda)\vert Q_x\vert\xi(\lambda)\rangle$ with $\xi(\lambda)=e^{-iH_R\lambda}(\Psi_b\otimes\chi)$; for a pair $s_x=\gamma_1\langle Q^{(1)}_x\rangle+\gamma_2\langle Q^{(2)}_x\rangle$.

$\lVert R_f(\lambda)\rVert_1\le8\lVert C_{bf}\rVert^2\lvert\lambda\rvert$ with $\lVert C_{bf}\rVert\le\lvert\gamma\rvert(\mu_{N-1}+\tau)\max_x\lVert\Phi_x\rVert$; the view differs from its $G_f$-evolution by at most $4\lVert C_{bf}\rVert^2\lambda^2$.

$G_f$ is independent of $\lambda$ iff $\Gamma_
u=0$ for every Bohr frequency $
u
eq0$ of $H_R$; true for every start in one eigenspace of $H_R$, and in coupling (c) with all $\Phi_x$ equal and $\kappa=0$ or $X\chi=0$ for every start.

Control: on a ring with $\kappa=0$ the start $\frac1{\sqrt2}(\lvert p\rangle_n\beta_{k,+}(p)+\lvert0\rangle_n\beta_{k,+}(0))\lvert f_k\rangle$, $\sin p\neq0$, has a source field oscillating at frequency $\omega_k(p)-M_k$ in both couplings, so $G_f$ depends on $\lambda$ whenever $\sum_xe^{ipx}\Phi_x\neq0$.

Branch start ($\sigma=\pm1$, level $k$, label $p$; $\kappa=0$ or $X\chi=0$): $S^{(a)}_{k,\sigma}=\gamma\sigma M_k^2/\omega_k(p)$, $S^{(c)}_{k,\sigma}=\gamma\sigma\omega_k(p)$, $\omega_k=\sqrt{M_k^2+\tau^2\sin^2p}$; constant in $\lambda$; records give a correction of first order in $\kappa$ at fixed $\lambda$.

$S^{(c)}=\gamma L_b$, $S^{(a)}=\gamma M_k^2/L_b$ with $L_b=\langle C_{\rm D}\rangle=\sigma\omega_k(p)$; a relation to the listed body term, not invariant under moving single-body operators into $C_{\rm D}$.

Pair in an eigenvector of $C_{\rm pair}$ on fixed levels: $S^{(a)}_{12}=\sum_i\gamma_iM^{(i)}_{k_i}\langle\sigma^{(i)}_3\rangle$, $S^{(c)}_{12}=\sum_i\gamma_i\langle C_{{\rm D},i}\rangle$, equal to $\gamma(E_{12}-\langle U\rangle)$ for $\gamma_1=\gamma_2=\gamma$; the binding term contributes no term of its own.

Control: for $U=u\sigma^{(1)}_1\sigma^{(2)}_1$ at $p_1=p_2=0$ the pair presents $(\gamma_1M^{(1)}_{k_1}+\gamma_2M^{(2)}_{k_2})M/\sqrt{M^2+u^2}$, different from the sum of the free sources when $u\neq0$ and $\gamma_1M^{(1)}_{k_1}+\gamma_2M^{(2)}_{k_2}\neq0$.

The replacements leaving $C$ unchanged are exactly moves of single-object operators (constants, place-dependent, internal) between the terms containing the object; $C_{\{b,f\}}=\gamma\sum_xQ_x\otimes\mathring\Phi_x$ is fixed by $C$.

$G_f$ modulo $\mathbb 1_f$ equals $\operatorname{Tr}_R((\lvert\xi\rangle\langle\xi\rvert\otimes\mathbb 1)C)$ and is fixed by $C$ and the start to first order; the split into $C_f$ and a body part is not, and without a form rule $s_x$ is fixed only up to state-independent shifts.

For $\gamma\neq0$ and some $\mathring\Phi_y\neq0$: a constant added to $\sigma_3\otimes(m\mathbb 1_N+D)$ is a convention iff all $\mathring\Phi_x$ are equal; otherwise the zero of the body operator is fixed by $C$.

Reading the source from a listing of form (a) or (c): if some $\mathring\Phi_x\neq\mathring\Phi_y$, the source field, its total and its ratio to another body are well defined (the first two up to a common factor $1/a$); if all $\mathring\Phi_x$ are equal, none is, and only differences $S-S'$ between starts of one body (and their ratios) are.

open_issues: M_k is taken as μ_k = m + d_k, the half-gap of the on-site block; the question does not quote its definition.
Normalized branch starts are taken on a ring or as packets; boundary corrections for long open chains are not estimated.
With records (κ > 0, Xχ ≠ 0) only a bound on the change of the total source is given; the O(κ) correction is not computed.
The common factor 1/a (normalization of the Φ_x) and which field descriptions fix it are left to the packages on the field's response and profile.
For the pair only eigenvectors of the pair contract and one control are treated; no general relation between the pair's source and those of its free parts.
